# porkbun_tld_registration_requirements (Data Source)

Reads Porkbun's machine-readable registration requirements for one TLD: whether it can be registered through the API at all, the term and contact rules it imposes, and the JSON Schema of the registrant data it demands.

This is account-independent — it describes a TLD, not a domain you own — so it can be read before anything is registered.

`request_schema` and `registry_requirements` are whole JSON Schema documents, which have no fixed shape, so they are returned as JSON **strings**. Read them with `jsondecode()`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# What .com asks of a registrant, and what .us asks on top of it.
data "porkbun_tld_registration_requirements" "com" {
  tld = "com"
}

data "porkbun_tld_registration_requirements" "us" {
  tld = "us"
}

# Both schema attributes are JSON documents in a string, and both are null
# when Porkbun sent no schema — so guard every jsondecode with a null check.
output "com_create_fields" {
  value = data.porkbun_tld_registration_requirements.com.request_schema == null ? [] : keys(
    jsondecode(data.porkbun_tld_registration_requirements.com.request_schema).properties
  )
}

# Null whenever the TLD has no structured eligibility rules, which is most.
output "us_eligibility_fields" {
  value = data.porkbun_tld_registration_requirements.us.registry_requirements == null ? [] : keys(
    jsondecode(data.porkbun_tld_registration_requirements.us.registry_requirements).properties
  )
}

# A hard gate: this fails the apply when Porkbun cannot register the TLD
# through the API. A `check` block would only warn and let the apply finish.
resource "terraform_data" "com_is_api_registerable" {
  input = data.porkbun_tld_registration_requirements.com.tld

  lifecycle {
    precondition {
      condition = data.porkbun_tld_registration_requirements.com.api_registerable
      error_message = format(
        ".%s cannot be registered through the Porkbun API: %s",
        data.porkbun_tld_registration_requirements.com.tld,
        coalesce(data.porkbun_tld_registration_requirements.com.not_api_registerable_reason, "no reason given"),
      )
    }
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `tld` (String) The top-level domain to describe, without a leading dot, e.g. `com`, `us`, `co.uk`. Lowercase, with no surrounding whitespace.

### Read-Only

- `api_registerable` (Boolean) Whether this TLD can be registered through the API. False for TLDs whose registry eligibility data the API cannot submit; those must be registered on porkbun.com.
- `max_registration_years` (Number) The longest term the registry allows, in years. **Null means Porkbun stated no maximum**, which is not the same as a stated `0`.
- `not_api_registerable_reason` (String) Why the TLD is not API-registerable. Null when `api_registerable` is true, and when Porkbun gave no reason.
- `registrant_only` (Boolean) Whether the TLD uses only the registrant contact, with no separate admin, tech or billing contacts.
- `registration_duration_years` (Number) The fixed term, in years, that the API registers this TLD for.
- `registry_requirements` (String) A second JSON Schema document, in a string, enumerating the extra registry eligibility fields the TLD requires — `.us` purpose and category, `.ca` legal type — with their allowed values, human labels and an `x-policyNote`. **Null when the TLD has no structured extra requirements**, so `registry_requirements != null` is the test for "this TLD asks for more". These fields document eligibility; `/domain/create` does not accept them today.
- `request_schema` (String) The `/domain/create` request body this TLD accepts, as a JSON Schema (Draft 2020-12) document in a string. Pass it to `jsondecode()`. Null if Porkbun sent no schema.
- `requires_validated_address` (Boolean) Whether the registry requires a validated registrant address. Registrations for these TLDs can come back asking for an address correction to be confirmed.
- `whois_privacy_supported` (Boolean) Whether WHOIS privacy can be enabled for this TLD.
